traits.notes: The seedling displays pinnately compound leaves with opposite leaflets. The leaves are clustered at the branch tips. The overall appearance suggests a young tropical tree seedling. Some leaflets show minor damage (small holes).

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (clearly visible in multiple images where leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped in dense clusters at the ends of the branches)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (individual leaflets are clearly visible attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf structure terminates in a single terminal leaflet)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (based on the most complete visible leaf structures)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval with the widest point near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (the base of the leaflets appears broadly rounded)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a distinct central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and well-spaced (secondary veins are clearly visible and curve towards the leaf margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces reflect light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles appear relatively short compared to the leaf blade size)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the young stems appear green and flexible, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stems appear smooth without visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: green (stems are predominantly green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stems appear smooth without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the leaflets)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: The seedling displays pinnately compound leaves with opposite leaflets. The leaves are clustered at the branch tips. The overall appearance suggests a young tropical tree seedling. Some leaflets show minor damage (small holes).
